correctness.rationale: The earliest-greedy endpoint formula holds by induction for every finite word. In a palindrome, reverse modular jumps sum to q for distinct symbols and 2q for repeats; the middle even pair contributes q. Counting distinct first halves with e repeats gives exact coefficients. Summing first-appearance thresholds over n yields the rational bivariate identity, and its positive root gives the growth limit. Each boundary n=0, odd length 1 and even length 2 is included. Independent subsequence-set brute force passed 56 prefixes/430 cells and 1915 greedy-endpoint comparisons; finite tests corroborate rather than replace the all-length argument.

value.rationale: The all-q>=3, all-length joint distribution of distinct scattered palindromes for a canonical balanced periodic family is a motivated natural invariant in a field where general results emphasize maxima/length bounds. Exact rational bivariate enumeration and a sharp q-dependent growth base are substantive beyond isolated finite calculations, while not making an unsupported all-host generalization.
